item.title: BVI Vacation Without Sailing Experience: Best Yacht Charter Options for Beginners
item.description: Picture waking up to the sound of waves against the hull of a catamaran anchored in a secluded cove in the British Virgin Islands (BVI). Walk on deck and soak up the sunshine and the spectacular views this area is famous for. It’s the perfect holiday, and the best part is that no sailing experience is needed. With Dream Yacht Worldwide , you can enjoy a BVI yacht vacation without having to know a jib from a mainsail. We make sailing accessible to all, with three options especially suited for beginners: Easy Crew, Skippered, and Cabin Cruises. Can You Go on a BVI Vacation Without Sailing Experience? Many people assume that exploring the ocean requires a formal captain’s license or a deep understanding of marine navigation. While renting a boat entirely on your own, known as a bareboat charter , requires sailing experience, there are plenty of ways to enjoy the sea without any technical knowledge. With a crewed BVI sailing vacation , you don’t need to stress about managing a vessel. Our team oversees managing the necessary tasks, such as tracking the weather, anchoring in a busy bay, or interpreting complex nautical terms. You’ll have experienced staff managing onboard systems for you while you enjoy the experience. Our modern catamarans are also stable boats, which means a very low risk of motion sickness and a comfortable stay for those new to life on the water. Best BVI Charter Options If You Don’t Know How to Sail Every traveler has a different preference when it comes to privacy, budget, and daily schedules. Dream Yacht Worldwide provides three distinct entry points designed to match your personal style. Best For Privacy Level Meals Budget Skippered Charter Families and friend groups High (Full private yacht) Cook your own meals or dine ashore Mid to High Easy Crewed Charter Milestone trips and relaxation seekers High (Full private yacht) Half or full board cooked by a host Premium Cabin Cruise Couples, solo travelers, and budget travelers Private cabin, shared deck Set meal plan included in the price Affordable BVI Skippered Yacht Charters: Ultimate Freedom and Privacy A skippered charter means you rent an entire yacht for your group and hire a professional captain to sail it. You have total control over your daily schedule, allowing you to choose exactly when to sail and which bays to visit. The captain handles all the physical labor, anchoring, and navigation, while you and your guests enjoy the exclusive use of the boat. A BVI catamaran charter with skipper is ideal for families who want to cook their own meals or try local beachside restaurants every night. BVI Crewed Yacht Charters: The Effortless Private Getaway If you want the ultimate luxury of a private boat combined with the service of an all-inclusive resort, consider an Easy Crewed charter . Along with a professional captain, you get a dedicated onboard host/cook to manage the galley and handle tasks like grocery shopping (provisioning) or cooking meals during your stay. Cabin Cruises: The Budget-Friendly Entry Point to Sailing A Cabin Cruise is a smart choice for those who want to experience the yachting lifestyle without renting an entire boat. You can book an individual, private cabin with its own bathroom on a large, modern catamaran. The journey follows a pre-planned route, and meals are prepared and served by the crew. Think of it as staying at a boutique hotel that drops anchor at a different, beautiful spot every day. Why the BVI Is Ideal for First-Time Yacht Vacations The British Virgin Islands are widely considered the sailing capital of the Caribbean. The unique geography of the region creates a gentle, welcoming environment for anyone new to the water. Line-of-Sight Navigation and Calm Waters One of the biggest comfort factors in the BVI is that you can almost always see the next island on the horizon. Because the islands form a protected channel, the water remains remarkably calm and sheltered from large ocean swells. This visual navigation removes…

item.title: What’s a Cabin Cruise? Everything You Need to Know Before Booking
item.description: Imagine waking up to the sound of water gently lapping against the hull, stepping outside, and diving straight into a clear, turquoise ocean. For a long time, enjoying a holiday like this meant you either needed a lifetime of sailing experience or the budget to rent a whole private vessel with a captain. Now, travelers can book a cabin cruise and experience the magic of a sailing vacation to an exotic destination for the price of a single hotel room. Even better, sailing experience is not required. You simply book your cabin, step aboard, and leave the work to the crew on board the yacht. Before you pack your bags and head for the marina, here is everything you need to know about this effortless way to explore the world. What Is a Cabin Cruise? A cabin cruise, also called a by-the-cabin sailing charter , is a style of travel where you rent a private stateroom or cabin on a yacht. The rest of the vessel is shared with a small group of like-minded travelers, so you have opportunities to socialize in between exploring islands and relaxing in your room. Every cabin charter trip features a carefully planned route, shared communal spaces, delicious meals, and a professional crew to run the ship. It’s an easy way to dip your toes into the yachting lifestyle. What Is a Cabin Charter Like? The entire travel process is designed to be stress-free from the moment you book your cabin cruise vacation to the day you head home. Choosing Your Destination and Dates Your journey begins by selecting where you want to sail and picking the dates that fit your schedule. These trips follow set itineraries, which you can view ahead of time. This way, you can see which ports you’ll visit and plan ahead of time. Arrival and Boarding When you arrive at the marina base, the crew will welcome you aboard and show you to your private stateroom. After a quick safety briefing and an introduction to the yacht, the captain casts off the lines and sets sail. Your Cruise Each day follows a relaxing rhythm of sailing, swimming, exploring hidden coves, and enjoying fresh meals on deck. While the captain handles the sailing, you share the spacious decks with your fellow passengers. Do You Need Sailing Experience? With this type of sailing vacation, no experience is required. You do not need to know how to tie a single knot, read a navigation chart, or handle a steering wheel. The price of your cabin includes the services of the captain and crew. They take care of navigation, weather tracking, anchoring, and all daily shipboard operations. The only thing you need to do the entire week is relax and have fun. What’s Included in a Cabin Yacht Charter? Inclusions vary based on the package you choose and the company you book with. Premium options, such as Dream Yacht ’s cabin cruises, typically include: A private, comfortable double cabin with its own bathroom Access to all shared yacht spaces, like the forward trampolines, salon, and sun decks The full services of a professional captain and cook Onboard water toys, which may include things like snorkeling gear, paddleboards, and kayaks Before booking, be sure to check the trip details to confirm inclusions and what you might need to cover during your cruise. Food, Beverages, and Culinary Options Many packages offer a half-board plan, which includes select meals such as breakfast and lunch. With half-board options, you may dine ashore at ports where you drop anchor. Other packages feature a full-board plan, which means breakfast, lunch, and dinner are included. Optional Excursions and Extras Depending on where you are sailing, you might have the option to add on excursions like guided island hikes and historical tours. It is always a good idea to check your specific package details before booking, so you know exactly what is covered and what extras you might want to explore. item.title: What I Learned From Our One-Year Sailing Sabbatical
item.description: Chris DiCroce is an Amazon bestselling author, sailor, online educator, and speaker. He’s been featured in Sail Magazine, The Waterway Guide, Spinsheet Magazine, and various other magazines and podcasts. He spent 6 years cruising various parts of the U.S. and the Western Caribbean with his wife and dog, and 2 years traveling through Guatemala and Mexico. To learn more about Chris and his travels, visit mondovacilando.com . Read about his experience living on a yacht below… Have you ever wondered what it would be like to take a one-year sailing sabbatical and sail away from it all? Do you find yourself watching countless YouTube videos featuring bronze bodies and beautiful sailboats anchored in the turquoise waters surrounding some faraway island? I know exactly how you feel. For years, I also dreamt of warm breezes and salty waves. After a stream of layoffs at my job left me searching for answers, I decided to go for it. The only thing that needed to happen in order for this dream to become reality was to convince my wife Melody to get onboard – literally. After many late-night discussions, we came to the conclusion that life is short. Time is precious. We said, “What good is having a dream if you never go for it?” So, on a glorious weekend, I, Melody, and our dog Jet loaded up our 35-foot sailboat and hit the high seas for what was to be our one-year escape. Casting Off the Dock Lines We sailed south along the east coast of the United States, bound for Cuba and the Western Caribbean. Once the butter started to melt, we knew we were closer to our ideal latitude. We adjusted quickly to our new life. The concerns we had about the lack of space or how Jet would adapt to life on a sailboat faded. As a matter of fact, when we saw the sun rise over the city of Havana, any remaining doubts about whether our sailing sabbatical was the right decision drifted off with the seafoam. It was a morning we’ll never forget. Cuban immigration officials were both shocked and amused that we were sailing with a 50 lb. dog. They had a lot of questions about how and where he goes to the bathroom. Of course we all had a good laugh as Melody and I tried to explain, in our mediocre Spanish, that getting Jet to go on deck was proving to be a test of wills. But once the officials were satisfied we had all the correct paperwork and international health certificates, Jet got his stamp of approval. We spent fourteen days exploring Havana’s bustling streets. We discovered quaint local eateries, amazing art galleries, and off-the-beaten-track neighborhoods. When we left, we sailed west along the north coast in some of the bluest water I’ve ever seen. We anchored in deserted bays and sipped our Havana Club rum as we watched the sun tuck itself in for the night. We crossed the Yucatan Channel and spent three incredible weeks anchored in the Makax Lagoon in Isla Mujeres. We learned a little more Spanish and immersed ourselves further into our cruiser personas. In our minds, a one-year sailing sabbatical wasn’t much time. We wanted to experience as much as possible, so we moved often. And we kept moving. We kept exploring. We sailed south to Belize, where we snorkeled the out islands and took in the spectacular reef that is second only to the Great Barrier Reef of Australia. Melody and I were in the water at dawn and in our bunk before 9. Sailing With a Dog Jet seemed to love his new aquatic life as well. I mean, who wouldn’t love long strolls on deserted beaches and endless belly rubs from strangers in the beach bar? But sailing with a dog presents some challenges. He’s a shepherd and he sheds a lot, therefore, we vacuum constantly. And yes, there’s the bathroom issue on longer passages. Jet refused to use the fake grass pad that we put on deck for his potty breaks. He gave in a few times when there was no alternative, but more often than not, we planned our route and our stops so that it afforded us the ability to land a dinghy and take him to shore. item.title: Hotspots for scuba diving in Thailand
item.description: While Thailand may be best known for its tropical climate, white sand beaches, rich culture and delicious cuisine, scuba divers know it as a world-class diving and snorkeling destination. The stunning waters of Thailand are home to over 300 islands, 1200 miles of coastline and hundreds of incredibly diverse dive sites. From impressive wrecks to pristine reefs to colorful coral-encrusted walls, scuba diving in Thailand will delight every diver from novice to expert. One of the most exciting ways to experience diving in Thailand is from aboard a private sailing charter, where you can avoid the crowded day charter boats and dive directly from your liveaboard yacht. The Dream Yacht Charter base is located in Yacht Haven Marina on the island of Phuket that extends down into southeast Thailand’s Andaman Sea – where most of Thailand’s top dive and snorkeling spots can be found. Scuba diving in Thailand is known and loved for exceptional underwater visibility, varied marine life and some of the best coral to be found anywhere in the world. And if you’re anything like the many divers looking to experience a thrilling dive with whale sharks and manta rays, the Andaman Sea can provide the dive experience of a lifetime. When putting together your itinerary for scuba diving in Thailand, consider the time of year, your dive experience, and the types of activities you enjoy most – whether you want to swim with tiger sharks, snorkel along scenic beaches, or macro dive and linger among rare tiny sea critters. When diving the Andaman Sea, visiting between October and April is ideal, when seas are calmer and visibility is at its best. To help you plan, we’ve put together our list of favorite hotspots for scuba diving in Thailand. Read on to find your diving bliss! Phi Phi Islands A NOVICE DIVERS PLAYGROUND The Phi Phi Islands are stunningly beautiful both above and below the surface. With its sparkling bays and crescent beaches surrounded by stunning rock formations, it’s one of the most photographed areas of Thailand. It’s worth a visit for the above-water scenery alone, but for divers the underwater experience is a must. With striking coral gardens, caverns, and swim-throughs, along with calm novice-friendly bays, it offers some of the most thrilling diving for beginners. Keep an eye out for leopard sharks that are often seen here. Koh Phi Phi is also a great option for those interested in snorkeling in Thailand. Check out the main island of Koh Phi Phi Don for amazing snorkeling at both Nui Beach and Long Beach. Phuket CONVENIENT GATEWAY TO THAILAND DIVING Phuket is often overlooked when considering the many options for scuba diving in Thailand. But Phuket’s coastline offers a surprising variety of dives with dramatic underwater landscapes, excellent visibility and easy conditions. And it’s one of the best places in Thailand for those interested in shore diving for beginners. Visit the popular Koh Dok Mai dive site to see extraordinary yellow tube corals and numerous eels. More experienced divers will enjoy Shark Point, known for beautiful leopard shark sightings. Richelieu Rock AN ADVANCED DIVER’S PARADISE Some say the Richelieu Rock dive site offers the best scuba diving in Thailand. This pinnacle site is located north of the Similan Islands, and is fairly remote, taking a bit longer to reach. But it’s well known for whale shark sightings, with the best time of year to spot them being between February and May. And even if you don’t spot the whale sharks, Richelieu Rock has much more to offer, including manta rays, walls of yellow anemones, and macro critters like sea horses, and porcelain crabs. Keep in mind that Richelieu Rock is best for advanced divers, due to the open water swells and strong currents.
